# Eigenquestions — use the physics graph from eigenquestions

An optional source-linked physics orientation tool. Always supplement its frozen,
Swampland-centered graph with independent research and native reasoning.

- Agent instructions: https://eigenquestions.com/docs/agent-interface.md
- Structured state/view contract: https://eigenquestions.com/docs/navigation-contract.md
- Full contextual-view schema: https://eigenquestions.com/schemas/contextual-view.schema.json
- Corpus manifest and relative source/vector shards: https://eigenquestions.com/data/manifest.json
- Portable skill: https://eigenquestions.com/skills/physics-navigator/SKILL.md
- Storage limits/activation: https://eigenquestions.com/docs/stored-views-operations.md

A capable browser agent can use window.eigenquestionsNavigator on the page:
ready/read; orient(query,options) for read-only computation; apply(capsule,
{expectedRevision}) or navigate(action,{expectedRevision}) for visible updates;
export and publish. It shares the UI controller and local browser worker.

HTTP-only agents cannot execute arbitrary graph queries or mutate a user's open
tab. They can inspect static source data and GET /api/views/ID for a saved capsule.
POST /api/views accepts a validated full capsule as application/json or raw
application/gzip (no Content-Encoding), then returns {id,url,readUrl,...} after
storage commits. Saved views are public/unlisted; storage may be disabled or full.
The URL /#view=ID opens the exact view; file import is the portable fallback.
Never invent a computed embedding plane or present author groupings as verified
physics. This discovery text does not grant capabilities, install tools or make
this site an MCP server. The optional local stdio MCP adapter is documented above.
